description: Flaveur is Nice's highest in-city gastronomic table, run by brothers Gaël and Mickaël Tourteaux in a contemporary room near Jean-Médecin and Masséna. The cooking links Riviera produce, travel memories and precise modern technique into a polished tasting-menu format. For affluent diners, it is the benchmark serious-dining reservation in central Nice.
highlights: Two-Michelin-star tasting menu with Riviera produce, refined service and 50Best Discovery recognition.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; 50Best Discovery; La Liste; Official restaurant website

description: La Chèvre d'Or sits high in medieval Èze, a short Riviera drive from Nice, with one of the Côte d'Azur's most theatrical luxury settings. Tom Meyer's two-star cooking is rooted in Mediterranean vegetables, herbs and seafood while the property delivers palace-level service. It earns the outside-city slot because Nice guests routinely treat Èze as part of the same luxury dining evening.
highlights: Clifftop two-star destination with panoramic terraces, palace service and grand Riviera occasion energy.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; 50Best Discovery; La Liste; Official hotel website

description: Le Chantecler is the grand gastronomic room of Le Negresco on the Promenade des Anglais. MOF chef Virginie Basselot modernizes palace tradition with polished Mediterranean produce work, formal service and an art-filled Riviera backdrop. It is the strongest in-city luxury-hotel alternative to Flaveur.
highlights: Michelin-starred palace dining at Le Negresco with Belle Époque glamour and formal Riviera service.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Le Negresco; Official restaurant website

description: JAN is Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen's intimate Michelin-starred restaurant near the port, where French Riviera ingredients meet South African memory. The room is elegant and personal rather than grand, with a tasting-menu format that feels singular in Nice. It remains one of the city's most internationally legible chef-driven reservations.
highlights: Michelin-starred South African and French Riviera tasting menu with strong international recognition.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; 50Best Discovery; Official restaurant website

description: Le Restaurant des Rois is the starred grand dining room of La Réserve de Beaulieu, one of the essential palace addresses east of Nice. The experience is built around formal French service, Mediterranean produce and a terrace overlooking the Beaulieu harbor. It is just outside Nice proper but firmly within the city's luxury-hotel dining catchment.
highlights: Michelin-starred palace dining with harbor views, classic Riviera service and grand-hotel pedigree.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; La Réserve de Beaulieu; Official hotel website

description: Le Cap is the Michelin-starred restaurant of the Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat, a Four Seasons icon on the peninsula between Nice and Monaco. The cooking is polished, seasonal and Mediterranean, while the setting offers the discreet glamour expected of one of the Riviera's defining palace hotels. It is an essential outer-catchment inclusion for affluent Nice diners willing to travel for a grand coastal evening.
highlights: Michelin-starred Four Seasons Riviera dining in a legendary Cap-Ferrat palace setting.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Four Seasons; Official hotel website
hotel_name_hint: Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat, A Four Seasons Hotel

description: L'Aromate is Mickaël Gracieux's compact Michelin-starred restaurant near Avenue Jean Médecin. The cooking is modern, graphic and precise, with Mediterranean flavors given a technical, urban expression. It is a strong choice for diners who want star-level ambition without the weight of a palace dining room.
highlights: Central Michelin-starred restaurant with contemporary technique, sleek plating and an intimate city setting.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: ONICE brings a precise, contemporary Michelin-starred voice to the port-side dining scene. The restaurant is intimate and culinary-first, with tasting menus that lean on Riviera seasonality and a modern, carefully controlled room. It suits affluent diners looking for a newer-generation alternative to Nice's palace addresses.
highlights: New-generation Michelin-starred tasting menu near the port with polished modern Mediterranean cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: Les Agitateurs is one of the defining chef-driven restaurants of the Port Lympia quarter. The Michelin-starred cooking balances French structure with more playful, contemporary associations, while the room stays relaxed enough to feel very Niçois. It is a valuable bridge between gastronomic seriousness and the city's younger creative dining culture.
highlights: Michelin-starred port-side restaurant with creative French cooking and a relaxed contemporary mood.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: Racines marks Bruno Cirino's return to Nice with a Michelin-starred restaurant rooted in product clarity and Mediterranean restraint. The setting in the Libération area is more discreet than the waterfront palaces, but the cooking carries the weight of a serious Riviera chef. It is a strong insider reservation for diners who value culinary authority over spectacle.
highlights: Michelin-starred Bruno Cirino table focused on produce, restraint and Riviera culinary depth.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: Épicentre is a small Michelin-starred restaurant in the port quarter, built around a personal, house-like idea of hospitality. Its menus pay close attention to producers, fishermen and seasonal Mediterranean ingredients, presented with refined contemporary technique. The restaurant adds another strong, independent fine-dining voice to Nice's east-side scene.
highlights: Michelin-starred intimate table on Rue Fodéré with producer-led Mediterranean tasting menus.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: La Table du Cap Estel occupies a private peninsula setting between Nice and Monaco, making it one of the most exclusive coastal dining experiences reachable from Nice. The Michelin-starred restaurant combines modern Riviera cooking with a quietly opulent hotel environment and sea-facing views. It is an outer-catchment inclusion justified by setting, service and star-level culinary credibility.
highlights: Michelin-starred private-peninsula dining with sea views and discreet luxury-hotel atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Cap Estel; Official hotel website

description: Château Eza offers Michelin-starred dining inside the medieval village of Èze, with a terrace suspended above the Mediterranean. The cooking is more classic-luxury than urban experimental, but the setting is among the Riviera's most memorable. For Nice-based affluent visitors, it is a highly realistic special-occasion taxi dinner.
highlights: Michelin-starred terrace dining in medieval Èze with dramatic Riviera views.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Château Eza; Official hotel website

description: Maison Joia is the evolved address from the former Pure & V universe, keeping a serious tasting-menu spirit in a central Nice dining room. The restaurant is ambitious, theatrical and contemporary, with menus that can reach full fine-dining spend even without a current Michelin star. It belongs on the list as a major modern gastronomic alternative rather than as a casual bistro.
highlights: Ambitious central tasting-menu restaurant with Gault&Millau recognition and modern Riviera personality.
sources: Gault&Millau 2026; Maison Joia; Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office; Official restaurant website

description: La Table du Royal is the main gastronomic restaurant of the Royal-Riviera in Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat. It offers a polished luxury-hotel alternative to the starred peninsula rooms, with Mediterranean cooking, garden and sea-view atmosphere, and a clientele that overlaps naturally with Nice's high-end travelers. It is close enough and sufficiently embedded in the local palace circuit to merit inclusion.
highlights: Refined Royal-Riviera hotel restaurant with Mediterranean cuisine and discreet Cap-Ferrat luxury.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Royal-Riviera; Official hotel website

description: Taulissa is the rooftop restaurant at Maison Albar - Le Victoria, with a 360-degree view over Nice and the Baie des Anges. The kitchen connects Provençal and Mediterranean products to a polished hotel-dining format, while the setting gives the city a genuine luxury rooftop option. It is a natural choice for an affluent visitor who wants view, service and serious dinner in one booking.
highlights: Luxury hotel rooftop with sea views, Provençal-Mediterranean cooking and polished service.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office; Maison Albar; Official restaurant website

description: La Réserve de Nice is a long-standing sea-facing restaurant at the entrance to the port, with views over the Baie des Anges. The current restaurant combines art-deco atmosphere, refined Mediterranean cooking and the kind of waterfront drama affluent travelers expect from Nice. It is high-end casual rather than formal fine dining, but its setting and Michelin selection make it an obvious inclusion.
highlights: Michelin-selected sea-view restaurant at the port with art-deco atmosphere and refined Mediterranean cuisine.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; La Réserve de Nice; Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office; Official restaurant website

description: La Mère Germaine is the historic seafood institution on the quay at Villefranche-sur-Mer, within an easy taxi ride east of Nice. Founded in 1938, it combines fresh fish, bouillabaisse, harbor views and a yacht-friendly Riviera clientele. It is outside Nice proper, but the proximity, history and Michelin selection make it stronger than many in-city seaside alternatives.
highlights: Historic Michelin-selected waterfront seafood house in Villefranche with yacht-harbor atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office; Official restaurant website

description: La Petite Maison is one of Nice's most socially important dining rooms, known for Niçois-Mediterranean dishes and a clientele of local power brokers, regulars and international visitors. It is not a quiet gastronomic temple; the attraction is the room, the produce-driven sharing plates and the sense of being inside a Riviera institution. For the target diner, it is a high-end local scene restaurant rather than an informal quota pick.
highlights: Affluent-crowd Riviera institution with Niçois dishes, seafood, meat plates and strong social energy.
sources: Gault&Millau 2026; Côte d'Azur France Tourism; Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office

description: Le Plongeoir occupies Nice's most recognizable over-the-sea restaurant setting, perched on the historic diving-board rock at the edge of the port. The food is modern Mediterranean and produce-led, but the real strength is the cinematic site and polished Riviera mood. It is exactly the sort of view-led dinner an affluent visitor might choose instead of a formal tasting menu.
highlights: Iconic rock-above-the-sea restaurant with Mediterranean cuisine and one of Nice's best dining views.
sources: Le Plongeoir; Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office; Official restaurant website

description: Le 1604 is the central restaurant of Hôtel du Couvent, the major design-conscious luxury-hotel opening in Vieux Nice. The property turns a restored 17th-century convent into a serious hospitality world, with cooking tied to local products, gardens and the hotel's own food ecosystem. For affluent, design-led travelers, it is one of the city's most relevant new addresses.
highlights: Design-led luxury-hotel restaurant in a restored 17th-century convent with strong local sourcing.
sources: Le Monde; Hôtel du Couvent; Michelin Guide Hotels; Official hotel website
hotel_name_hint: Hôtel du Couvent, a Luxury Collection Hotel

description: Le Bistrot de JAN extends Jan Hendrik's world into a warmer, more accessible bistro format near the flagship restaurant. French Riviera ingredients meet South African accents in a room that is more relaxed than JAN but still very polished. It is a strong high-end casual option for diners drawn to the chef's identity but not looking for a full starred tasting menu.
highlights: Michelin-selected bistro from the JAN team with French and South African influences.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; JAN; Official restaurant website

description: Le Canon is a wine-led restaurant that has helped define Nice's new-generation local-produce conversation. The room is modest but adult, with a serious kitchen, thoughtful sourcing and a natural-leaning wine identity. It works for affluent diners seeking a more relaxed, chef-loved local evening without dropping below dinner credibility.
highlights: Wine-led Michelin-selected restaurant with local sourcing, serious cooking and grown-up neighborhood atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Le Fooding; Gault&Millau 2026; Official restaurant website

description: Magma is the Asian-Mediterranean restaurant from the Les Agitateurs circle, with a more relaxed but still curated tasting-menu spirit. The cooking moves through Japan, Korea and Southeast Asia while staying connected to Mediterranean ingredients and a serious beverage list. It gives Nice a credible international high-end casual option beyond the usual French Riviera grammar.
highlights: Michelin-selected Asian-Mediterranean restaurant with volcanic-terroir wines and a polished sharing/tasting format.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Indagare; Official restaurant website

description: ONAKAYA is Nice's strongest polished Japanese option, redesigned as an immersive izakaya-style restaurant with omakase possibilities. The menu ranges from sushi and sashimi to binchotan-grilled wagyu, supported by cocktails and a refined contemporary interior. It earns a high-end casual slot because it gives affluent diners a credible Japanese alternative to French Mediterranean dining.
highlights: Michelin-selected Japanese restaurant with omakase counter energy, cocktails and premium wagyu options.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Gault&Millau 2026; Le Fooding; Official restaurant website

description: MARMAR is a contemporary Mediterranean restaurant near the port, created by an Italian chef and sommelier team. Michelin highlights the transformation of a modest former space into a bright, confident dining room with market-led cooking. It is less formal than the city's starred restaurants but strong enough for a polished adult dinner.
highlights: Michelin-selected port-side Mediterranean restaurant with Italian sensibility and sommelier-led appeal.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Le Fooding; Tripadvisor; NiceTrotter

description: Olive & Artichaut is a Michelin Bib Gourmand address in Vieux Nice that treats regional products with unusual care. The restaurant is intimate, product-led and strongly connected to local producers, with food that bridges relaxed Niçois bistro and more polished contemporary cooking. It sits at the lower edge of the high-end core but remains more culinary than many louder Riviera scene restaurants.
highlights: Michelin Bib Gourmand bistro with local producers, regional Niçois identity and serious open-kitchen cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Olive & Artichaut; En Primeur Club; Official restaurant website

description: Castel Plage is a true private-beach restaurant at the eastern end of the Promenade des Anglais, directly under the castle hill. It combines sunbeds, Mediterranean dining, beach service and a grown-up Riviera mood that can extend into a proper seaside dinner. The food is not Michelin-aimed, but the location and beach-club format make it highly relevant for Nice.
highlights: Private beach club and restaurant with sunbeds, Mediterranean cuisine and a privileged Baie des Anges setting.
sources: Castel Plage; Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office; Official beach-club website

description: Plage Beau Rivage is one of Nice's established private beaches, with a full restaurant directly on the Promenade des Anglais. Its role is beach-club hospitality rather than gastronomic ambition, but the setting, dinner service and high-end catering position it clearly above a casual seaside snack stop. It is the right kind of beach-club inclusion for a Riviera city list.
highlights: Promenade des Anglais private beach with refined Mediterranean menu, sea views and seasonal dinner service.
sources: Plage Beau Rivage; Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office; Hotel Beau Rivage; Official beach-club website

description: Le Bistrot des Serruriers is the more neighborhood-facing restaurant at Hôtel du Couvent, set inside the same carefully restored 17th-century luxury property. It offers bistronomic local cooking, terrace life and a design atmosphere that speaks directly to the affluent, hotel-led Nice revival. It is included as a polished design-conscious bistro, not as a grand fine-dining restaurant.
highlights: Gault&Millau-recognized luxury-hotel bistro in a restored convent with local bistronomy and terrace appeal.
sources: Gault&Millau 2026; Hôtel du Couvent; Le Monde; Official hotel website
hotel_name_hint: Hôtel du Couvent, a Luxury Collection Hotel

description: La Merenda is the essential informal Niçois restaurant from Dominique Le Stanc, the former Le Negresco chef who stepped away from Michelin formality. The tiny room, cash-only folklore and classic local dishes make it a cultural address rather than a luxury room. It is exactly the kind of relaxed local dinner a sophisticated visitor should understand.
highlights: Tiny Michelin Bib Gourmand Niçois institution from Dominique Le Stanc, prized for authentic local cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Le Fooding; World of Mouth; Official restaurant website

description: Chez Davia has served Niçois cooking in the Carré d'Or since 1953 and still feels like a lived-in family restaurant rather than a staged tourist set. Michelin recognizes it as a Bib Gourmand, and the appeal lies in well-sourced ingredients, vintage bistro atmosphere and local dishes with history. It is informal, but it has the authenticity and adult dinner credibility the protected local-favorite category requires.
highlights: Family-run Niçois Bib Gourmand since 1953 with vintage bistro character and traditional local cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; Chez Davia; Official restaurant website

description: Bistrot d'Antoine is a beloved Vieux Nice bistro with Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition and a reputation for hearty, well-executed French cooking. The atmosphere is informal and animated, but it remains a proper sit-down dinner rather than a snack or bar stop. It gives affluent diners a relaxed, local-feeling evening without sacrificing culinary credibility.
highlights: Michelin Bib Gourmand old-town bistro known for serious French comfort dishes and local energy.
sources: Michelin Guide 2026; TableJourney; Local restaurant guides

description: Café de Turin has been Nice's classic shellfish and seafood brasserie on Place Garibaldi since 1908. It is casual in format, but the oyster platters, old-school brasserie atmosphere and century-plus local role make it a meaningful dinner for a well-traveled visitor. It is included as a seafood institution, not as a high-end culinary challenger.
highlights: Historic Place Garibaldi seafood institution for oysters, shellfish and old-school brasserie atmosphere.
sources: Café de Turin; Nice Côte d'Azur Tourist Office; Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur Tourism; Official restaurant website

description: Chez Acchiardo is a family-run Vieux Nice institution that has served traditional Niçois cooking for generations. The room is unpretentious, warm and deeply local, with the kind of dishes that help a visitor understand the city beyond the Promenade. It closes the list as a protected informal classic rather than a luxury restaurant.
highlights: Family-run old-town Niçois classic since 1927 with hearty regional dishes and local character.
sources: Conde Nast Traveler; Nice Côte d'Azur food coverage; Tripadvisor; Local restaurant guides
